status: Team-approved authored operational rubric; not a certification or instructor-defined scoring threshold

dimensions.name: Leadership and sponsorship
dimensions.evidence_questions: Accepted charter, outcome, sponsorship, decision rights and escalation support. A title or enthusiasm does not establish funding/access/launch authority.

dimensions.name: Skills and training
dimensions.evidence_questions: Demonstrated operational, domain, evaluation, technical and incident competence with coverage for the stage. Assess supported internal or external capability rather than requiring an internal engineering team.

dimensions.name: Workflow and process
dimensions.evidence_questions: Reviewed procedures, baseline, responsibilities, handoffs, exceptions and fallback. A proposed application boundary or discussion invitation does not prove current workflow understanding.

dimensions.name: Infrastructure and data
dimensions.evidence_questions: Permitted usable records, identity/timestamp handling, representative quality checks, interfaces, access tests, logging and recovery. Neither engineers nor cloud/ERP ownership alone demonstrates this.

dimensions.name: Resources and budget
dimensions.evidence_questions: Authorized funding and staff time for integration, use, review, correction, monitoring, maintenance and contingency within the stage/horizon. Separate budget approval, authority evidence, new spending and production commitments.

dimensions.name: Governance and risk
dimensions.evidence_questions: Applicable approvals, enforced authority limits, rehearsed escalation, incident handling and stop responsibility appropriate to exposure. Review policy alone does not demonstrate control effectiveness.

dimensions.name: Culture and change
dimensions.evidence_questions: Affected-user involvement, legitimate concerns, workload/incentive effects and feedback route. Do not assume acceptance, resistance or motives from size or posture.

dimensions.name: Operating ownership
dimensions.evidence_questions: Accepted accountable business/service ownership, technical support, monitoring, incident/escalation coverage, maintenance and exit for the assessed stage. A project sponsor is not automatically the service owner.

overall_labels: Ready to proceed to the next management gate
aggregation: No numeric composite, average or count-based cutoff. Explain materiality, consequence and dependencies. Critical blockers cannot be offset by unrelated strengths.

priority_tiers.P0: A condition required before the requested stage; retain as blocking until evidenced.
priority_tiers.P1: Another material dependency with explicit stage/timing; all essential conditions still block.
priority_tiers.P2: Justified later improvement, not a generic checklist.

unknown_rule: Do not convert absent evidence into confirmed absence. Report known blockers and unknowns together. A critical unknown blocks unconditional readiness for the affected stage; explain why lesser unknowns do or do not affect a narrower stage.
funding_rule: Preserve stipulated budget approval as a distinct fact. Unknown approver identity/delegation evidence does not prove no budget. Request role, scope, limit and effective date before new spend/change/expansion. Disputed or unverified authorization leaves affected actions blocked.
stage_rule: Critical controls must be demonstrated before exposure requiring them. A separately permitted offline rehearsal may investigate unproven controls with adequate containment and ownership. Preparation is not permission for live use. Pilot readiness is not production readiness.
output_contract: Use unchanged frozen schemas; detailed fields are labeled text within existing string fields.
